blocks.text: 14. Temperance
The Great Alchemist
Numbered fourteen, Temperance depicts a winged angel, often identified as Michael, pouring liquid between two cups.
Unlike Death, which was a sudden severance, Temperance is a slow, deliberate process of integration.
This is the archetype of Alchemy—the art of blending opposites (fire and water, spirit and matter) in perfect proportion to create a third, higher substance.
It teaches that true power lies not in force, but in the subtle mastery of balance.
The Union of Elements
The angel stands with one foot on solid earth and the other submerged in flowing water.
This posture signifies the bridging of the conscious (earth) and subconscious (water) realms.
On the angel’s chest is a square containing a triangle, representing the spirit contained within matter.
The fluid flowing between the cups defies gravity, suggesting that this is a magical act where spiritual laws supersede physical ones.
It represents the "middle way," avoiding the extremes of asceticism and indulgence.
The Principle of Moderation
Temperance embodies the principle of moderation, known to the Greeks as the "Golden Mean."
It is not about abstinence, but about correct use.
It suggests that any virtue pushed to an extreme can become a vice.
The card asks for adjustment, accommodation, and the careful management of resources.
It is the steady hand that mixes the volatile ingredients of life without causing an explosion.
The Agency of Healing
The agency of this card is healing and regeneration.
After the radical surgery of Death, Temperance is the convalescence.
It is the soothing balm that restores equilibrium to the system.
It represents patience, knowing that some chemical reactions cannot be rushed.
It teaches us to "temper" our steel—heating and cooling it repeatedly until it becomes both hard and flexible.
An Invitation to Blend
Drawing Temperance is a call to find your center.
It asks you to verify if your life is out of balance—are you working too hard? Loving too obsessively? Thinking too rigidly?
It invites you to mix a little water with your wine, to dilute your intensity with calm.
It is a reminder that the solution to your problem is not more effort, but a better mixture of ingredients.
